parts.text: What happens to the air pressure between the sheets while he blows?

options.text: Pressure between the sheets becomes lower than the pressure on their outer sides.
Pressure between the sheets becomes higher than the pressure on their outer sides.
Pressure between the sheets stays equal to the pressure on their outer sides.

parts.text: Give one reason that explains why the sheets move toward each other.

stem: Siddharth holds two light paper sheets hanging a few centimetres apart. He blows a fast stream of air between them. The sheets move toward each other.

part_answers.answer: Fast air between the sheets has lower pressure, so higher pressure on the outer sides pushes the sheets together.

teacher.key_rationale: High-speed air between the sheets lowers pressure there; higher outer pressure pushes the sheets together.
